> **Model C — Administrative Units scoped by facet tuples (per [ADR-078](../../adr/adr-078-orgpath-attribute-schema-15-facet.qmd)).** AU membership rules compose facet predicates from the 15-slot model rather than `-startsWith` on a composite-hyphen path. See [OrgPath Codebook](codebook.qmd) for the facet/slot definitions.

## The Delegation Problem

In Active Directory, delegation was implicit. Place a user in an OU, grant an admin group permissions on that OU, and delegation was done. The OU tree *was* the delegation model — every branch of the hierarchy defined a scope of management authority.

Entra ID has no OUs. It has a flat directory where every user is at the same level. Without a replacement for OU-based delegation, organizations face two bad choices:

1. **Over-delegate**: Give administrators tenant-wide permissions (Global Admin, User Admin) because there is no scope boundary. This violates least-privilege and creates audit findings.
2. **Under-delegate**: Lock down all administration to a tiny team, creating bottlenecks where every password reset, group change, and user update requires a central IT ticket.

Administrative Units (AUs) solve this — they create virtual scope boundaries within the flat directory. Under Model C, the boundary is defined by **facet tuples** (one or more `(attr, value)` predicates AND'd together), not by position in a composite path. The Delegation Matrix (UIAO_154) names the canonical AUs, their facet scopes, and the role assignments they carry.

## Three-Tier Model

| Tier | Scope | Who | What They Can Do |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tier 1** | Enterprise | Security team, Compliance, Executives | Read-only visibility across all governed principals |
| **Tier 2** | Department / Division | Department administrators | Full user lifecycle management within their facet scope |
| **Tier 3** | Sub-team (Department + Division + Role tier) | Helpdesk / per-team admins | Password resets and basic user support within their narrow facet scope |

Each tier maps to an Administrative Unit whose membership rule cites one or more facet values from the codebook:

- **Tier 1:** `AU-Enterprise` — every principal with at least one declared facet
- **Tier 2:** `AU-Department-IT` — `(attr2 -eq "IT")`
- **Tier 3:** `AU-IT-CyberOps` — `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "CyberOps")`

## Administrative Unit Registry

### Enterprise AU (Tier 1)

| AU | Rule | Restricted |
|---|---|---|
| `AU-Enterprise` | `(user.onPremisesExtensionAttributes.extensionAttribute2 -ne "")` | Yes |

The Tier-1 enterprise AU uses the Department facet's non-empty check as the canonical "is this principal governed by OrgTree?" predicate — populated Department implies the principal has been HR-provisioned through the OrgPath pipeline.

### Department AUs (Tier 2)

| AU | Rule | Department | Restricted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AU-Department-IT` | `attr2 -eq "IT"` | IT | Yes |
| `AU-Department-HR` | `attr2 -eq "HR"` | HR | Yes |
| `AU-Department-Finance` | `attr2 -eq "Finance"` | Finance | Yes |
| `AU-Department-Legal` | `attr2 -eq "Legal"` | Legal | Yes |
| `AU-Department-Engineering` | `attr2 -eq "Engineering"` | Engineering | Yes |
| `AU-Department-Operations` | `attr2 -eq "Operations"` | Operations | Yes |

| `AU-Department-Executive` | `attr2 -eq "Executive"` | Executive | Yes |

### Division AUs (Tier 3 — created on demand within a Department)

| AU | Rule | Scope | Restricted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AU-IT-CyberOps` | `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "CyberOps")` | IT/CyberOps | Yes |
| `AU-IT-InfraOps` | `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "InfraOps")` | IT/Infrastructure | Yes |

| `AU-Legal-GRC` | `(attr2 -eq "Legal") and (attr3 -eq "GRC")` | Legal/GRC | Yes |

### Cross-cutting AUs (facet compositions)

| AU | Rule | Scope | Restricted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AU-Region-NCR-Privileged` | `(attr1 -eq "NCR") and (attr10 -eq "Privileged")` | NCR privileged-access accounts | Yes |
| `AU-Cleared-TopSecret-Plus` | `attr9 -in ["TopSecret","TS_SCI"]` | Top-secret cleared personnel | Yes |
| `AU-Contractor-Active` | `(attr6 -eq "Contractor") and (attr8 -eq "")` | Active contractors (empty TermDate) | Yes |

## Role Assignment Matrix

| Role | Assigned To | Scoped To | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Global Reader | `OrgTree-IT-CyberOps-Users` | `AU-Enterprise` | 1 |
| Security Reader | `OrgTree-Legal-GRC-Users` | `AU-Enterprise` | 1 |
| Reports Reader | `OrgTree-Department-Executive-Users` | `AU-Enterprise` | 1 |
| User Administrator | `OrgTree-Finance-Admins` | `AU-Department-Finance` | 2 |
| Groups Administrator | `OrgTree-Finance-Admins` | `AU-Department-Finance` | 2 |
| User Administrator | `OrgTree-HR-Admins` | `AU-Department-HR` | 2 |
| User Administrator | `OrgTree-IT-Admins` | `AU-Department-IT` | 2 |
| Helpdesk Administrator | `OrgTree-IT-CyberOps-Admins` | `AU-IT-CyberOps` | 3 |
| Password Administrator | `OrgTree-IT-CyberOps-Admins` | `AU-IT-CyberOps` | 3 |
| Authentication Administrator | `OrgTree-IT-InfraOps-Admins` | `AU-IT-InfraOps` | 3 |
| Conditional Access Administrator | `OrgTree-IT-CyberOps-Admins` | `AU-Cleared-TopSecret-Plus` | (cross-cutting) |

Notes:
- The `*-Admins` dynamic groups derive from the corresponding `*-Users` groups via a separate membership rule (typically an enriched HR attribute or a manually curated list per UIAO_154).
- Cross-cutting AUs (like `AU-Cleared-TopSecret-Plus`) get role assignments only when the operational need crosses Department/Division boundaries (e.g., a CISO-led security-clearance review).

## Restricted Management

**Every AU in this matrix is Restricted Management.** This is non-negotiable.

Restricted Management means:

- Global Administrators **cannot** manage AU members without explicit AU-scoped role assignment
- Only users with roles scoped to the specific AU can manage objects within it
- This **prevents privilege escalation** — even a Global Admin cannot bypass facet-scoped delegation

An unrestricted AU is classified as **CRITICAL drift** and triggers immediate remediation.

## Drift Detection

| Drift Type | Severity | Auto-Fix |
|---|---|---|
| AU Membership Drift — rule mismatch (per-facet clause) | HIGH | Yes |
| Role Assignment Drift — unauthorized assignment | CRITICAL | No — investigate |
| Unrestricted AU — missing Restricted flag | CRITICAL | Yes |
| Orphaned AU — no role assignments | LOW | No — flag |
| Missing AU — canonical entry with no tenant AU | HIGH | Yes |
| Stale facet citation — rule references a facet value not in the codebook enumeration | HIGH | No — fix codebook or rule |

The per-facet drift model (see [Drift Detection Walk-through](drift-walkthrough.qmd)) classifies AU rule drift per clause: if `(attr2 -eq "IT") and (attr3 -eq "OldDivision")` references a now-deprecated `OldDivision` value, the second clause surfaces independently as a phantom-facet finding while the first clause continues to validate cleanly.
